extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting nonfiction book proposals to Storey Publishing or Timber Press (gardening, horticulture, crafts, nature, home reference, cooking, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting nonfiction book proposals (gardening, crafts, nature, home reference, cooking, etc.) to Storey Publishing and Timber Press, including required proposal components, marketing information, and submission method constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / topic fit (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of Storey Publishing is to serve our customers by publishing practical information that encourages personal independence in harmony with the environment. The books we select include nonfiction titles for adults and children on gardening, home reference, crafts, cooking, beer & wine, nature, raising animals, horses, building, farming, homesteading, and mind/body/spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with this mission and subject list; Storey does not consider fiction, poetry, or children's picture books. Only proposals on the listed practical/nonfiction topics are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited genres (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: no fiction, poetry, or children’s picture books, please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit proposals outside allowed nonfiction categories; submissions in prohibited genres will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of introduction (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include a letter of introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a brief cover letter that introduces yourself and your project; this is part of the required submission packet.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-paragraph book description (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-paragraph description of your book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the book succinctly in a single paragraph to convey concept and hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need and audience statement (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief statement explaining why you think your book is needed and describing the potential readers of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the gap your book fills, target readership, and why the topic matters to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable titles with differentiation (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of recent books (if any) similar to your own, with a thorough explanation of how yours will be different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name similar works and clearly explain distinguishing features of your proposal (content, approach, audience, scope, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents with chapter descriptions (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of contents, including a brief description of each chapter, including a complete list of projects, if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chapter-by-chapter breakdowns and list project content for craft/how-to books so editors can evaluate structure and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format/length/illustration plan (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your thoughts about the length, format, and photographic/illustrative requirements of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss estimated length, desired trim/format, number/type of photos or illustrations, and whether you will provide or commission artwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author bio emphasizing credentials and promotion (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bio with a focus on your credentials for writing the book and your ability to promote it to a wide audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight subject-matter expertise, publishing or media experience, platform, and promotional activities that increase the book's marketability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample chapter (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample chapter from the proposed book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a representative chapter to demonstrate writing style, voice, organization, and level of detail. No specific length limit provided, but choose a chapter that best showcases the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft-book samples (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: For craft books, please include photographs or samples of a few projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear photos or physical samples (as specified) to demonstrate project quality, design, and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and return of materials (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: Email your proposal to submissions@storey.com. Or send by mail to: Editorial Department, Storey Publishing LLC, 210 MASS MoCA Way, North Adams, MA 01247 (Enclose a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you would like your materials returned.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storey accepts proposals by email or postal mail; include SASE if you want materials returned by post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time expectation (Storey)
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the number of submissions we receive, it may take several months for us to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect a long lead time before hearing back and should not expect rapid replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview / project uniqueness (Timber Press)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview: Tell us what is unique about your project. Discuss your overall approach and proposed organization. Define your intended audience and explain why the book will appeal to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a clear case for the book's unique angle, organization, and target market; explain why readers will buy it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents and representative sample chapter (Timber Press)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of Contents: List all chapters, along with any front matter (introduction, preface) and back matter (appendices, charts, references, bibliography, index). Briefly describe what is contained in each chapter. Provide a representative sample chapter of no more than 10 pages in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full TOC with chapter descriptions and a concise sample chapter (<=10 pages) that showcases the manuscript's tone and level of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author information / qualifications (Timber Press)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author Information: Summarize your familiarity with the subject and explain why you are qualified to write the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate subject expertise, credentials, and relevant experience that position you to author the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales and marketing plan / platform (Timber Press)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sales and Marketing: Describe your marketing platform (how your social media and professional activities and contacts will aid the promotion of the book). If you give lectures or workshops, include a summary of your activities for the past year. Please describe your current social media outreach with any applicable links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete metrics and examples of audience reach (social links, lecture counts, workshop history) and how you'll support sales efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing / comparable titles with specifics (Timber Press)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing/Comparable Titles: List any books published in the past five years that address the same subject as your book and describe how your book differs. For each title, include publisher, publication date, price, and Amazon ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit comparable-list to recent (past five years) titles and include bibliographic and marketplace details so editors can assess overlap and market positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript length, art plan, and image samples (Timber Press)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript Length and Illustrations: Give an estimated word count for your completed manuscript and a general art plan including photos, illustrations, maps, graphs, and/or diagrams that you feel are necessary to convey your ideas. If you are providing the photos or illustrations include samples of your work. If you will be working with a professional photographer, explain why they are well suited to the project and provide sample images or a link to their website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate final word count, describe required artwork and its role, and supply image samples or photographer credentials/links when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method constraint (Timber Press)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact Information: Submissions are only accepted via email. Please direct your proposal to editorial@timberpress.com
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timber Press requires email submissions only; do not send postal mail unless otherwise instructed.
